info.description:
The Media Collection API is a server-side, RESTful equivalent of the client-side Media SDK for tracking streaming audio and video in Adobe Analytics. A media session is composed on Adobe's servers from a `sessions` call followed by a series of `events` calls, which are aggregated into media metrics. 

 **Endpoint host:** The host is a provisioned endpoint of the form `<company>.hb-api.omtrdc.net`. Obtain your host from your Adobe representative. The `example.hb-api.omtrdc.net` host shown here is a placeholder. 

 **Content type:** All request bodies must be JSON. Set the `Content-Type: application/json` request header on every call. 

 Note: Adobe may add optional request and response members (name/value pairs) to existing API objects at any time and without notice or changes in versioning. If implemented properly, such additions are non-breaking changes for your implementation. Adobe will not remove parameters or add required parameters without first providing standard notification through release notes.
info.title: Media Collection API

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Send playback events to an active session.

tags.name: Schemas
tags.description: Retrieve the JSON validation schema for an event type.

post.description: Starts a new media tracking session with a `sessionStart` event. On success the response returns `201 Created` with the session path in the `Location` header. Parse the trailing session ID from that header and use it in all subsequent events calls. Your app calls this once at the start of a tracking session.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: A `sessionStart` event. The `params` object carries the required Analytics, visitor, and media parameters.

201.description: Session created. The session ID is returned in the `Location` response header.

Location.description: The relative path of the created session, in the form `/api/v1/sessions/{sid}`. Parse the `{sid}` segment and use it for events requests.

400.description: Bad request. The request body did not pass validation for the event type. See the JSON validation schema for the event type.

post.description: Sends a playback event (such as `play`, `ping`, `pauseStart`, `bufferStart`, `bitrateChange`, `chapterStart`, or an ad event) to an active session. The request body has the same structure as a sessions request. A successful call returns `204 No Content`; the endpoint does not return a body.

parameters.name: sid
parameters.description: The session ID returned in the `Location` header of the sessions request.

204.description: No content. The event was accepted successfully.

400.description: Bad request. The request had an improper format. Check the JSON validation schema for the event type.

404.description: Not found. The session ID was not found. Start a new session with the sessions endpoint.

410.description: Gone. The session is closed and can no longer report activity. Start a new session with the sessions endpoint.

get.description: Returns the publicly accessible JSON validation schema that the back end uses to validate the request body for a given event type. These schemas are the authority for which parameters are required or optional, and their data types.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description: The event type to retrieve the schema for, for example `sessionStart` or `ping`.

200.description: The JSON validation schema for the requested event type.

EventType.description: The media tracking event type sent on the wire.

PlayerTime.description: The playhead position and timestamp of the event. Required on every request.

ts.description: The client-side timestamp of the event, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Params.description: Analytics, visitor, and media parameters. The required members depend on the event type; see the request parameters reference and the JSON validation schema for each event type.

analytics.reportSuite.description: The Analytics report suite ID that receives the data.

analytics.enableSSL.description: Whether to send Analytics data over HTTPS.

visitor.marketingCloudUserId.description: The Experience Cloud ID (ECID) of the visitor.

visitor.aamLocationHint.description: The Audience Manager location hint (region) for the visitor.

media.id.description: The unique content ID for the media item.

media.name.description: The human-friendly name of the media item.

media.length.description: The length of the content, in seconds.

media.contentType.description: The content type, for example `vod` or `live`.

media.playerName.description: The name of the media player in use.

media.channel.description: The channel or property the content plays on.

QoeData.description: Optional quality-of-experience data. May be sent with any event.

media.qoe.bitrate.description: The current bitrate, in bits per second.

media.qoe.timeToStart.description: The time, in milliseconds, from the play request until playback started.

media.qoe.errorID.description: An identifier for a player error.

media.qoe.errorSource.description: The source of the error, for example `player`.

CustomMetadata.description: Free-form string key-value pairs. Sent only with the `sessionStart`, `adStart`, and `chapterStart` event types. All values must be strings.
